IPTW identification weights

Source: R/weights.R
dot-iptw_weights.Rd

Cluster-level inverse-probability weights (Leung 2025; Prop. weights (iv)): $$\beta_{ij}(\phi_1) = 1\{C_{N_{ij}} = 1\} / P(C_{N_{ij}} = 1), \quad \beta_{ij}(\phi_0) = 1\{C_{N_{ij}} = 0\} / P(C_{N_{ij}} = 0),$$ where the probabilities use the cluster-level assignment law (distC, paramsC) over the \(k = |N^{cl}_{ij}|\) distinct neighbouring clusters. Units whose neighbouring clusters are not all treated (for phi_1) or all control (for phi_0) get weight 0.

Usage

.iptw_weights(A, C, W_C, distC = "binom", paramsC = list(prob = 0.7))

Arguments

A

n_unit x n_unit adjacency matrix (with self-loops).

C

integer vector of cluster ids.

W_C

0/1 vector of cluster-level treatments, indexed by cluster id.

distC, paramsC

cluster-level assignment law.

Value

A list with numeric vectors weights1 and weights0.

Examples

A <- Matrix::Matrix(outer(1:12, 1:12, function(i, j) abs(i - j) <= 1) * 1,
                    sparse = TRUE)
C <- rep(1:3, each = 4)
W_C <- c(1, 0, 1)
w <- generalClusterExp:::.iptw_weights(A, C, W_C,
                                       distC = "binom",
                                       paramsC = list(prob = 0.7))
## nonzero only where the cluster neighbourhood is all-treated / all-control
cbind(phi1 = w$weights1, phi0 = w$weights0)
#>           phi1     phi0
#>  [1,] 1.428571 0.000000
#>  [2,] 1.428571 0.000000
#>  [3,] 1.428571 0.000000
#>  [4,] 0.000000 0.000000
#>  [5,] 0.000000 0.000000
#>  [6,] 0.000000 3.333333
#>  [7,] 0.000000 3.333333
#>  [8,] 0.000000 0.000000
#>  [9,] 0.000000 0.000000
#> [10,] 1.428571 0.000000
#> [11,] 1.428571 0.000000
#> [12,] 1.428571 0.000000
